title: Day 0 - Made a Promise
text:
“Nobody is going to look at my resume and just give me a job. There’s no way! I have to stand out.”
I said that to myself in the mirror this morning. It made me realize the truth.
Obviously, no one’s coming to save me.
No recruiter is going to slide into my inbox. Or will they? No clue And definitely I am not some god coder.
But I am just a guy who still wants to fight.

title: Day 0 - Made a Promise
text:
The Promise
So I said to myself that for the next 30 days, I am going to show up no matter what.
30 days. No excuses. Just show up.
Every single day, I said I will: - Learn something hard - Build something real - Write about it - Share the journey
Just showing up every. single. day.

title: Day 0 - Made a Promise
section: Why did I call it “30 Days of Hell Out There”?
text:
Why did I call it “30 Days of Hell Out There”?
Because honestly, it feels like hell right now. Very uncertain. Feeling lost

Not knowing where I stand

Feeling like I am falling behind

Waking up anxious

This blog — this whole series — is me swinging back.
Just wanted to document everything.

title: Day 0 - Made a Promise
text:
Inspired by the KING
It’s inspired by Virat Kohli — not just for the records, but for the mindset.

Ruthless discipline

Showing up when no one’s watching

Grinding when it’s hard

And proving yourself over and over again

That’s what I’m trying to tap into.

text:

title: Day 3 - Good Sleep, Good Learnings
text:
Needed to get some good quality sleep, so woke up with around 7 hours of sleep.
Finished my daily ritual.

Started off with the LC Biweekly Contest — 4 problems in total.
I was able to solve just the first one:

3587. Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Alternate Parity

Really liked the problem. Not trivial at all. I vaguely remembered a similar pattern from an earlier contest, but this one still took a lot of mental energy.
Nice way to activate the brain early in the day.

Watched the India vs England Test match for a bit.

Later, drew the system diagram for a personal side project I’m working on.
Mainly a learning project — no real-world use case, but focused on core concepts:

Kafka
Producers / Consumers
API Gateway
Docker Network
End-to-End Deployment
Microservices


Did a mock DSA interview with a friend, basic BFS stuff.
Struggled with it. Conceptually understood it, but actually writing the code was a whole different story.
It kind of put me in my place. Now I know where I stand.
No excuses, just gotta keep grinding and practicing. Nothing fancy, just consistent effort.
I keep reminding myself:

I need to struggle while learning. That’s when real learning happens.

Looking at solutions too early makes things feel deceptively easy. Need to stop that habit.

Did some basic chores since it’s the weekend: house + room cleaning.

Wanted to deploy my stuff on the Oracle VM I had set up earlier.
It was pretty barebones — had to do everything manually.
So I SSH’d in and went step-by-step:

Opened ports I wanted to expose
Installed apps
Updated system packages

Quick bash for that:
sudo yum update -y

yum (Yellowdog Updater, Modified) is a command-line package manager used on Oracle Linux to install, update, remove, and manage software packages.


Followed this guide to install Docker: https://collabnix.com/how-to-install-docker-on-oracle-linux-a-step-by-step-guide/
For docker-compose, used:
mkdir -p ~/.docker/cli-plugins/
curl -SL https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/download/v2.27.0/docker-compose-linux-aarch64 -o ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose
chmod +x ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose

Wrote the docker-compose.yml for my project and tested it locally, things ran well.
One thing I noticed:
Docker Compose doesn’t natively support waiting for services to be “ready” before starting the next ones. Might explore workarounds.
Also opened the necessary ports via the Cloud Console.
To start Docker engine:
sudo systemctl start docker

Deployed it all on the VM.
Yaaayyy. Lesssgoooo.
Tried setting up a simple frontend on Vercel but wasn’t able to hit the backend API. No idea why — leaving that for tomorrow.

Honestly, I’d say it was a semi-productive day.
But I definitely learned a lot.
Feeling good about how things are shaping up.
Let’s keep building.

title: Day 6 - Sleep Deprived but Still Going
text:
Woke up early but with a headache. Slept late last night but I was so used to my routine of waking up early, that I just woke up.
Guess I’m just going to be a little sleep deprived today.
Started off the day with the daily ritual.

Had to record a video for the hackathon submission.
Even though the deadline was yesterday, we were still allowed to make changes to the video.
Please feel free to check it out here → YouTube

Registered for a webinar with Confluent on Data Streaming with Apache Flink.
Now I finally understand what Flink is for and how it fits into the bigger picture.
Really insightful session with lots of key takeaways and learning.

Took 15 minutes to meditate - just helped center things a bit, I guess.

Spent time working on feedback for my PRs and addressing the report feedback from our mentor.
Tomorrow’s the final submission date for the data product and report, so I’ve just been finishing things up.
Wrapped up all the parts I was responsible for.

Got a pretty decent project idea today that I’m actually excited about.
Sketched out a very high-level design and the main components.
Planning to build a prototype by the weekend, let’s see how that goes.

Also, a small rant lol, my left Shift key stopped working properly. Very very annoying.
Had to do a couple more flow diagrams for the project report.
Now I should be done… hopefully.

Overall, a decent day.
Mostly report work, but the new project idea has got me hyped.
Now I have got something to look forward to.
Let’s build that shit!!!!!

title: Day 8 - Vibe Coding All Day
text:
Woke up late, I was super tired and needed more sleep and rest.
But woke up feeling really fresh.

Spoke to my parents for a bit and made some coffee.
Made a few updates to my resume.
Helped out a friend with some some work that he had to do.

Then got into building that project idea I have been working on.
Got a lot done today:

Built the consumer service
Tested it on Confluent Cloud, it worked fine, felt it was pretty straightforward
Then started working on the core logic of the app
Had to give a lot of thought on designing the core logic
Did a lot of intial analysis on the data and then finalised an approach
Streaming data is a bit tricky I guess

That part took a while.
Was deep in it for the rest of the day, just zoned in.

Overall, felt like a really productive day.
Just vibe coding and trying to build real use case projects.
So far so good. One day at a time.

title: Day 13 - Final Touches and CI/CD Feels
text:
Woke up early, even though I didn’t get enough sleep, definitely less than 6 hours.
But I was just looking forward to the day.
Immediately showered, made my morning coffee, and sat down to finish what I had been working on.

The first version of the project was mostly done, just some cleanup work left.
I added a basic feedback button where users can drop in their thoughts.
Simple, but useful. Didn’t take too long to get that in.

Also created a complete CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions.
Now the whole deployment process is automated, it is super convenient now.
The script is pretty robust, and I am honestly very happy with how it turned out.
Did some basic testing after that to wrap things up.

Drafted out a LinkedIn post to showcase the project, will post it tomorrow.
Let’s see how that goes lol

Also, just a random thought and note, I guess Kafka is a fascinating technology.
The way it’s built and how it works under the hood is just so cool.
Definitely planning to go deeper into it.

That’s it for today.
Not a lot, but something.

title: Day 11 - Match Day and Dream Team Vibes
text:
Woke up after a good night’s sleep.
Spoke to my uncle and parents for a while, then had to get ready for a cricket match.

The entire day was just cricket, no project work or learning.
It was hot and sunny.
Perfect weather for a cricket match.

The match was awesome, it was intense af.
We were put in to bat first, and we had a clear plan.
Everything went exactly as expected and we were pretty happy with our innings.
I couldn’t contribute much with the bat today, a bit disappointing.
But that’s okay. The team is amazing, and it just feels really good to be part of it.
I still owe the team a match winning innings definitely and I believe that I am capable of doing it.

We defended the target, but it was super tense.
Lots of turning points, literally nail biting stuff.
But the best part? It was a complete team effort.
Every single person stepped up. Very very grateful to be a part of it.

The part I loved the most came after the match, we just grabbed a beer, and our captain addressed the team.
Felt so good to be in that moment.
This is what we all play for, passion, camaraderie, and team spirit.
Everyone genuinely cares about the game and each other.
Dream team, fr.

It was a long, hot day. Out in the sun the entire time.
Came back totally exhausted and just crashed.
Awesome day.

title: Day 12 - Exhausted Body But Energized Mind
text:
I was feeling super exhausted, lazy, and sore af. My entire lower body was really sore.
Woke up, and immediately showered and brewed some much-needed coffee.

Started the day with a top priority task, my Work Permit application.
Took about an hour to fill out everything carefully.
Also organized all the required documents into a single folder.
Now it’s all ready. Just waiting on the Letter of Completion from the university.
Once that’s in, I should be good to go.

Grabbed lunch and then went to meet a professor friend.
He’s not actually teaching us, but more of a mentor and friend. I learn a lot just by conversing with him. So much knowledge about life in general.
It was great seeing him after a long time.
Spent about an hour at his place, just casual convos and chill vibes.
Didn’t stay too long since he was busy with work.

After that, headed to the beach.
The weather was perfect, it was sunny and peaceful.
Grabbed a couple of beers and just sat by the water.
Vancouver is so beautiful.
I really feel super grateful to be here.

Came back home and met our new roommate, today was his first day.
Spoke to him for a bit, seems like a chill dude.

Then got to work.
I badly wanted to finish the frontend, deploy it, and have everything running.
It turned into a long night and I had to work till 1 AM.
But it’s done! Deployed and working as expected. Lessssgooooo
I want to write a detailed technical blog post on the whole thing soon. Let’s see, how that goes. I’ll definitely do it.

Overall, a really good day.
Rest, sun, peace, progress and most importantly, I enjoyed it thoroughly and felt good before I went to sleep.

Finished my short daily ritual and jumped straight into a call with my friend to continue working on our hackathon project.
We wrapped things up and the product is fully functional now.
Big shoutout to my friend who built most of it. I helped out with the frontend, documentation, and final submission details.
We both feel really good about it. That’s what matters in the end, I guess, whether we win or lose, we know we tried.

After the call, I finished writing the final capstone project report and created a PR for it.
Can’t believe it’s the last week before I finish my master’s.

Then I worked on documenting the app we built for the hackathon, we needed it for the submission.
Also completed documentation for:

The hackathon project repo
One of my personal project repos

Updated my LinkedIn too with the new projects and added relevant keywords.

I have got my IELTS exam tomorrow.
Haven’t practiced anything at all, to be honest
Took a mock test just before dinner and did decently well, I guess.
Will take a couple more tomorrow. Should be enough, hopefully.

I guess not much real learning today. But I got stuff done.
Feeling good. Just gotta keep at it.
We got this!!!

title: Day 7 - Kafka, Cricket, and Confidence
text:
Woke up early ish and completed my daily ritual.

Jumped on a call with friends, just catching up and brainstorming new ideas.
Had to update some flow diagrams for the final report and was finally done with it.

Started working on the project idea I came up with yesterday.
Made pretty good progress:

Set up the entire producer service
Got it working and publishing messages to Kafka on Confluent Cloud
Used a good bit of reactive programming in the producer class

Thinking of writing a technical deep dive blog on this soon. Let’s see how it goes.
Next up: building the consumer. Planning to work on that tomorrow.

Went to cricket practice today, it had been a very long time.
Felt great to pad up and bat again. Played decently well.
Might even play a match this Sunday, let’s see how that goes.

Came home super tired. Crashed after dinner.

Overall, a productive and active day, I guess.
Feeling good. Obviously stressed as hell, but also feeling confident with some serious self-belief.
Let’s keep going, one day at a time. Progress. Every. Single. Day

title: Day 2 - Just One of Those Days I guess
text:
Woke up a little later than I wanted to.
Finished my daily ritual.

The first thing I did was try again to get a better compute instance. Yesterday was a mess, some region unavailability and all that bullshit.
Found a workaround today and finally got it provisioned. Set it up. Just need to actually use it now. No point spinning things up and letting them sit idle.

Felt like doing Stacks today. Specifically, Monotonic Stacks.
Worked on:

496. Next Greater Element I (easy)
503. Next Greater Element II
Asteroid Collision


Caught up with a friend and followed the India vs England Test match.
First match after Virat Kohli’s Test retirement, so that felt weird.
We also debugged a bunch of stuff that he built for the hackathon. Mostly brainstorming and fixing bugs. Took over 3 hours, but made good progress. The deadline’s almost approaching as well. He did all of the work, but happy to help with documentation and stuff.

Then I showered and got ready for college. Had a seminar session on campus. It got pretty late.
Long commute after that because had to come to my sister’s place.

Honestly, not super productive today. Spent over 4 hours just commuting, and the rest of the day was just kind of packed. Starving. Super tired, to be honest.
Still, it wasn’t a bad day. It was just a busy one.
Even on days like this, I’m still pumped to learn and build in the coming days.
Not trying to stress myself too much.
Let’s just keep moving.

title: Day 1 IT IS
text:
Woke up pretty early today and kicked things off with a small ritual I’ve been trying to stick to. Nothing fancy - just something to ground me before diving into the day.
Started the morning with a couple of Leetcode problems. I’m deep in the Graphs section right now and today was all about Topological Sort. Solved a few problems around that, especially the Course Scheduler problem - did it both using BFS and DFS approaches. That felt pretty solid.
Right now, the goal is consistency. Just trying to get to a point where these things feel like muscle memory.

I also spun up a cloud compute instance - used the free-tier option with an Ubuntu image. SSH’d into it, practiced some Linux commands, then shut it down.
It’s a small start, but I have a plan for how I want to use it. Let’s see where that goes.

During my bus ride, I watched a video on Hybrid Cloud Architectures and how Confluent handles Cluster Linking without relying on tools like MirrorMaker 2. That was interesting.
Also touched on replication patterns — just high-level stuff for now, but it’s starting to click.
There was this random but funny analogy they used:

Trying to drink soup with a spoon - pain to clean.
Switched to a fork — less mess, still bad.
Eventually just drank directly from the bowl.
LMAO.

We’ve all been there in one form or another.

Had my TA work today for Introduction to Software Engineering. I’m the Lecture TA for this term.
Today’s lecture went into Intellectual Property (IP) and some pretty fascinating case studies:

Reggie Brown vs Snapchat:
Brown came up with the original idea and claimed there was a verbal agreement.
Snapchat argued that ideas alone aren’t enough.
Legally, Snapchat won, though it was eventually settled. Wild stuff.
Licensing — here’s what I gathered:

MIT/MPL: Just needs attribution.
GPL / LGPL / MPL: Each has different levels of openness and restrictions.

The Amazon Elasticsearch licensing mess also came up.
And Google vs Oracle over Java: Learned something crazy, so APIs are considered uncopyrightable.
So while you can’t copy the actual source code, you can write your own implementation of the same idea. I was like, damnnnn!

Honestly, TAing this course is teaching me as much as I’m helping others. Very Grateful to the instructor for many reasons.

Later, I applied to a bunch of jobs. Fingers crossed. Trusting God!
Got my 30 minutes of reading in from DDIA (Designing Data-Intensive Applications).
Trying to make this a daily thing and doing weekly discussions with my friends to keep it in my brain.

Fun Fact: The term “NoSQL” was actually a hashtag that became popular on Twitter and then people just stuck to it. It actually means Not only SQL, lol


Finished my college work and headed back home. Closed the day by learning the basics of Java multithreading. Here’s what I covered:



What concurrency and multithreading actually are
Difference between:

Program
Process
Thread
Multitasking
Multithreading

Also got into Time Slicing and Context Switching

In Java, you can create threads using either the Thread class or the Runnable interface.



Thread t1 = new Thread();
t1.join(); // Main thread waits until t1 finishes
